$meta.note: The single concept list shown after every free-text block (order randomised per presentation). Labels are everyday English; `concepts` maps each option back to catalog concept_ids (packages/data/catalog/concepts.json, v2.0.0) so human selections and model selections share one response space. `kind`: "catalog" = maps to the catalog; "distractor" = deliberately not relevant to any scene in the corpus; "none"/"other" = the two special options. NEEDS AUTHOR REVIEW before launch.
labelRules: Name the property, never its effect: 'How strong gravity is', not 'Gravity pulling things down' — a label that states the causal direction coaches the normative answer.
One idea per label, no 'and' joining two claims (Adams et al. 2006).

Options merge catalog concepts ONLY where the lay idea is genuinely identical (the four per-axis mass variants; launch_position+release_height). Everything else is 1:1, so the concept-overlap metric resolves at catalog granularity.
Distractors are styled like the real options so they cannot be spotted by form.
